title: Sandiganbayan denies Marcoleta’s bail request in plunder case
summary: This means that Marcoleta will remain detained during his trial

blocks.text: Senator Rodante Marcoleta, accompanied by PNP Criminal Investigation and Detection Group personnel, leaves the anti-graft court Sandiganbayan on July 15, 2026, and will be brought to the Quezon City Jail in Payatas.
This means that Marcoleta will remain detained during his trial
MANILA, Philippines – The Sandiganbayan 3rd Division has denied the bail petition of Senator Rodante Marcoleta in his plunder case.
The 3rd Division justices unanimously voted to deny Marcoleta’s bail petition, which means that he will remain detained during his trial.
Plunder is a non-bailable offense. In cases like these, the accused needs to file a bail petition with the court and the prosecution will present evidence to block the bail.

The decision of the anti-graft court means the justices found that the evidence of guilt against Marcoleta is strong — the threshold of evidence required for bail petitions. This does not mean, however, that the lawmaker and his co-accused are already found guilty.
Plunder, which has a threshold of P50 million, is a corruption offense involving public officials.

The Office of the Ombudsman filed the case against Marcoleta in July, due to questions related to the P75-million campaign donations he received. Aside from plunder, the senator is also facing three counts of alleged violation of Presidential Decree No. 46 (receiving gifts).

These cases stemmed from Marcoleta’s campaign donations for his senatorial run in 2025. He declared P51 million as net worth that year, but spent P112 million for his campaign. He did not declare any poll contributions.
Later, Marcoleta himself confirmed in a television interview that he received P75 million in campaign donations, explaining that he received the money before the campaign period started.

The senator explained that he did not include this in his Statement of Contributions and Expenditures (SOCE) because he was not yet a candidate when got the money. At the time, however, he was sitting congressman.
Marcoleta has also been suspended as a senator since October 19 as plunder case carries the penalty of suspension of officials. – Rappler.com
